HALF THIS BOARD HAS NO CODE TO CONFORM, and the board says so itself. Its
own title reads '[not-implemented] the variant-picker half:
component.variants is always empty and addVariant/updateVariant/
removeVariant have no callers (ComponentManager.ts:320,331,347). The

The detach half is reached through the probe: three conditions gate it —
a saved component, an INSTANCE of it selected on canvas, and the design
system in `pro` mode (ComponentDetailScreen.tsx, DSModeContext) — and none
of the three can be arranged by clicking in the demo. The probe mounts the
real ComponentDetailScreen and AutoOpen presses its own Detach button, so
the dialog measured is the shipped one, not a re-creation.
THE COPY DRIFT boards.json recorded ('drift-detach-copy-rewritten') IS
FIXED and verified in the probe: title 'Detach from component?', body
'This copy stops receiving updates from "Menu card". The component itself
is untouched.', buttons 'Cancel' and 'Detach' — the board's four lines.
WHAT IS NOT CONFORMED, and why the board loses on it:
1170:4802 draws a 340-wide popover, 14/16 padding, 10px gap, 12px title,
11/16 body, and buttons at 12/7 with a 6px radius. The shipped confirm is
chrome-ui's ConfirmDialog -> Modal kind='question': 440 wide, 16px insets,
a 14/600 title and 28h buttons at 12/6 with an 8px radius. That geometry
is not a local choice — Modal.tsx records it as measured against
184:24, and the button figures agree with the design system's own Button
9:102 wherever a board instantiates it (641:2597, 642:3397, 642:3399).
So this frame's numbers are outvoted by ten nodes across nine boards, and
one confirm dialog cannot have its own dialect: ConfirmDialog is the
single home for every destructive confirm in the product.
Like 1170:4777 in the same family, this frame instantiates no component
from the file — every node is a raw rectangle — which is the signature of
a sketch rather than a composed design.
ONE NODE IS JOINED, and it is the one the two readings agree on: the
footer's 8px gap between Cancel and Detach (1170:4809). Thin on purpose —
asserting more would mean asserting numbers this surface has just argued
should not hold.
